ops.title: Grants replay 'could not read' refusals are snapshot admission-queue exhaustion, not a read budget
ops.body:
Observed 2026-10-02 (grants-core-3) replaying the monorepo Slack hook (slack_writes_need_permission) over the 206 MB root transcript 900424b6 with ~/.claude/scratch/release-v3/capt-hook-grants/grants-core-3/battery.sh.

18 parallel cold capt-hook run PreToolUse processes: 6 of 54 runs (2 per battery) refused with INCOMPLETE_MESSAGE. The raised error was SnapshotProtocolError 'snapshot bridge response does not match request', which hid the host's error frame: Bridge.__call__ (captain_hook/snapshots/client.py) treated any op=error frame as a mismatch. With the error text surfaced: 'captain: snapshot admission queue exhausted'.

Mechanism: a cold CLI reaches the host through capt-hook-host transcript-client (internal/hookd/snapshot_bridge.go), which admits every non-warm op as 'review': reviewSlots 1, reviewQueue 16 (internal/hookd/snapshot_owner.go:293-294). snapshotService.call rejects without waiting when the queue is full. 18 processes start together and send their first tail at once, so exactly 18-16=2 fail per battery. 15-wide batteries: 0 of 30 refused. Hooks dispatched by hookd workers use 'hook' admission (4 slots, 64 queue), so production needs 65+ concurrent snapshot calls to see this.

Not a read past a budget: every snapshot read in the grants path is windowed (tail 256 events for the root, tail_bytes 4 MiB for the lane). The one unbounded read is root_excerpt (captain_hook/transcripts.py), a Python scan of the whole root file, run 5 times per Slack-hook event (~0.17 s each on 206 MB, ~1 s under load); it never touches the snapshot host.
